parsed.study_design: Qualitative interview study using framework analysis and a Behaviour Centred Design theory-of-change framework
parsed.population_and_sample: 17 national-, state-, and district-level actors involved in the rural Swachh Bharat Mission, drawn from the national capital and four states
parsed.exposure: Institutional and administrative features of Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin), including political leadership, target-setting, accountability, monitoring technology, staffing, communications, financing, and recognition of officials
parsed.outcome: Household toilet coverage and use, open-defecation reduction, and administrative behaviours supporting sanitation delivery
parsed.rationale: The Methods section (p. 2) reports structured interviews with 17 programme actors and systematic framework analysis, establishing an identifiable qualitative empirical design. The Results and “Change in the state of the world” section (pp. 3–7) link political leadership, administrative accountability, monitoring, staffing, and communications to changed district implementation behaviour and reported increases in rural household toilet coverage and use. The study therefore directly examines institutional and governance mechanisms affecting household sanitation access.
